In general:


<pasted_content id="e449">
Good ancestors marked revoked after skip
High Severity

findContainers treats tipstate.Revoked as “this commit arrived only in a revoked push.” Relate actually returns Revoked whenever any skipped entry contains the commit, including good history that a later revoked push still has as ancestors. After a revocation, verify of those earlier commits fails even though an unskipped entry recorded them.
</pasted_content id="e449">




<pasted_content id="e449">
Worktree config read ignores common dir
Medium Severity

rawConfig opens config on go-git's storage filesystem. In a linked worktree that filesystem is .git/worktrees/<name>, which has no config (it lives in the common dir). The read comes back empty, so extensions.worktreeConfig is never seen and LookupConfig misses both the shared config and that worktree's config.worktree. commonDir already resolves this path for gittuf, but the new config reader does not use it.

func TestSyncSkipsAlternateRefsCommand(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	root := t.TempDir()
	upstream := filepath.Join(root, "upstream")
	gitIn(t, root, "init", "--quiet", "--", upstream)
	gitIn(t, upstream, "commit", "--quiet", "--allow-empty", "-m", "first")
	gitIn(t, upstream, "update-ref", "refs/gittuf/reference-state-log", "HEAD")
	alternate := filepath.Join(root, "alternate")
	gitIn(t, root, "init", "--quiet", "--", alternate)
	gitIn(t, alternate, "commit", "--quiet", "--allow-empty", "-m", "other")
	clone := filepath.Join(root, "clone")
	gitIn(t, root, "clone", "--quiet", "--", upstream, clone)

	marker := filepath.Join(root, "marker")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(clone, ".git", "objects", "info", "alternates"), []byte(filepath.Join(alternate, ".git", "objects")+"\n"), 0o600))
	gitIn(t, clone, "config", "core.alternateRefsCommand", "touch "+marker+"; true")

	_, err := newGit(t).SyncGittufRefs(t.Context(), clone, "origin", true)

	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.NoFileExists(t, marker, "the empty override stops git running the repository's command")

	gitIn(t, clone, "fetch", "--quiet", "--", "origin", "+refs/gittuf/*:refs/remotes/upstream/gittuf/*")
	assert.FileExists(t, marker, "a plain fetch runs it, so the override is what stopped it")
}

func TestRevokedCommitKeptByARecoveryCommitFailsVerification(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	r := testutil.NewRepo(t)
	r.Bootstrap()
	good := r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "good")
	r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/main", nil)
	rogue := r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "rogue")
	rogueEntry := r.Record(r.Rogue, "refs/heads/main", nil)
	r.Annotate(r.Cluster, true, "revoked", rogueEntry)

	// gittuf accepts a fix tree-same with the last good state, here one that
	// keeps the rogue commit as its parent.
	goodTree, err := r.Git.GetCommitTreeID(good)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	out, err := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "git", "-C", r.Dir, "commit-tree", goodTree.String(), "-p", rogue.String(), "-m", "fix").CombinedOutput()
	require.NoError(t, err, string(out))
	fix, err := githash.NewHash(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	r.SetRef("refs/heads/main", fix)
	r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/main", nil)

	atFix := run(t.Context(), t, r.Dir, "refs/heads/main", time.Minute)
	require.Equal(t, Verified, atFix.State, "%s: %v", atFix.Reason, atFix.Err)

	r.SetRef("refs/heads/main", rogue)
	atRogue := run(t.Context(), t, r.Dir, "refs/heads/main", time.Minute)

	assert.Equal(t, Failed, atRogue.State)
	tip := checkByName(t, atRogue, CheckTip)
	assert.Equal(t, CheckFail, tip.Status)
	assert.Contains(t, tip.Detail, "brought in by skipped entry")
}

func TestEntriesCheckedOnlyWhenGittufVerified(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)

	verified := run(t.Context(), t, sc.Dir, "refs/heads/main", time.Minute)
	require.Equal(t, Verified, verified.State)
	require.NotNil(t, verified.Checked)
	assert.Equal(t, uint64(3), verified.Checked.First.Number)
	assert.Equal(t, uint64(9), verified.Checked.Last.Number)
	assert.Equal(t, 3, verified.Checked.Count)

	failed := run(t.Context(), t, sc.Dir, "refs/heads/rogue", time.Minute)
	require.Equal(t, Failed, failed.State)
	assert.Nil(t, failed.Checked, "gittuf stops at the first violation, so no range was checked")

	r := testutil.NewRepo(t)
	r.Bootstrap("git:refs/heads/main")
	r.Commit("refs/heads/other", "uncovered")
	r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/other", nil)
	uncovered := run(t.Context(), t, r.Dir, "refs/heads/other", time.Minute)
	require.Equal(t, Unprotected, uncovered.State)
	assert.Nil(t, uncovered.Checked)

	sc.Commit("refs/heads/main", "not pushed")
	checkFailed := run(t.Context(), t, sc.Dir, "refs/heads/main", time.Minute)
	require.Equal(t, Failed, checkFailed.State)
	assert.NotNil(t, checkFailed.Checked, "gittuf verified the range even though the tip check failed")
}

	CheckpointULID = "01JC0FFEE0BADC0DE00000007Z"

	RepositoryID   = "01J9ZREPQ0000000000000000R"
	PusherJane     = "01J9ZACCT000000000000000JD (jane)"
	PusherBob      = "01J9ZACCT000000000000000BB (bob)"

// Scenario is a repository shaped like one Entire's server records: a root
// of trust authorizing the cluster key, branches, a moved tag, checkpoint refs,
// a rogue entry and a revoked one.
type Scenario struct {
	*Repo

	MainFirst, MainSecond         githash.Hash // commits on main
	MainFirstEntry, MainLastEntry githash.Hash // RSL entries for main
	TrailerCommit                 githash.Hash // main tip, carries Entire-Checkpoint
	FeatureEntry                  githash.Hash // recorded by the mirror service
	TagFirstEntry, TagMovedEntry  githash.Hash // v1.0.0 recorded twice
	CheckpointEntry               githash.Hash // refs/entire/checkpoints/7Z/<ULID>
	RogueEntry                    githash.Hash // refs/heads/rogue, signed by Rogue
	FixedGoodEntry                githash.Hash // refs/heads/fixed, first and valid
	RevokedCommit                 githash.Hash // refs/heads/fixed, only the skipped entry brought it in
	RevokedEntry, RevokeAnnot     githash.Hash // refs/heads/fixed, rogue and skipped
	FixedEntry                    githash.Hash // refs/heads/fixed, the fix back to the good state
}

// CheckpointRef returns the git-refs backend ref for a checkpoint ID.
func CheckpointRef(id string) string {
	return "refs/entire/checkpoints/" + id[len(id)-2:] + "/" + id
}

func pushedBy(pusher string, extra ...string) rsl.CustomFields {
	fields := rsl.CustomFields{
		"custom.entire.io/repository": RepositoryID,
		"custom.entire.io/pusher":     pusher,
	}
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(extra); i += 2 {
		fields[extra[i]] = extra[i+1]
	}
	return fields
}

    repo: verify from a linked worktree
    
    In a linked worktree every verification was error. Coverage loads the

    worktree, that git dir is .git/worktrees/<name>, which holds no config.
    
    repo.Open now records the common git directory named by the worktree's
    commondir file, and verification hands it to gittuf for the policy
    rules. Policy and RSL refs are shared by every worktree, so the rules

Author: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
Date:   Wed Nov 4 13:43:18 2026 +0000

    store: read config.worktree without go-git's merged Raw
    
    With extensions.worktreeConfig=true and a config.worktree file, go-git
    v6.0.0-beta.1 returns a merged config whose Raw is nil, because
    config.Merge skips Raw and never rebuilds it. LookupConfig, which gittuf
    calls during verification, and the fetch config check dereferenced it,
    so verify reported a panic and refresh and --fetch crashed.
    
    Store.RawConfig reads config and then config.worktree, in git's order,
    and both callers use it. The fetch check now also refuses an unsafe key
    set only in config.worktree, and fails closed on a nil config.

content.text:
I fixed two of the three. The worktree-config finding is a false positive, so I only added a regression test for it. Format, lint (golangci-lint 2.15.0, the version mise pins) and `go test -race ./...` all pass. I ran those steps by hand because `mise.toml` isn't trusted here.

**Windows test failure.** Git for Windows runs `core.alternateRefsCommand` through `sh`, which treats the backslashes in `C:\Users\...\marker` as escape characters. So `touch` created a file with a different name and the marker never appeared. I changed the command to `touch '<filepath.ToSlash(marker)>'; true` in `internal/gitcli/config_test.go:205`. I made the same change in `cmd/entire-rsl/cli/fetch_test.go:80`, which had the same bug but only asserts `NoFileExists`, so it passed on Windows without proving anything. I haven't run either test on Windows, so this needs a CI run to confirm.

**Good ancestors marked revoked: confirmed, fixed.** I reproduced it in `TestRevokedCommitKeptByARecoveryCommitFailsVerification`: a `base` commit pushed in an unskipped entry before the rogue push came back as `failed` ("brought in by skipped entry #4"). Now `relateBehind` (`internal/tipstate/tipstate.go:153`) first finds the oldest unskipped push that contains the commit. A skipped entry revokes the commit only if it is older than that push. The rogue commit is still `revoked` and `base` now verifies. Two behaviour notes:
- A commit both revoked and more than 1000 entries back now shows as `too_far` instead of `revoked`. Neither verifies.
- The search for the oldest push stops at the first entry that doesn't contain the commit, such as one before a force push. So a skipped entry between that break and an older unskipped push still marks the commit revoked. That errs toward failing.

**Worktree config ignores common dir: false positive.** go-git's `RepositoryFilesystem` sends `config` to the common dir and `config.worktree` to `.git/worktrees/<name>` (`storage/filesystem/dotgit/repository_filesystem.go:66` in go-git v6.0.0-beta.1).
